column1: # Arabic-derived names as adapted by different Nigerian traditions.
# WHY THIS IS SEPARATE FROM hausa_variants.tsv
#   That file holds transliteration spread within one tradition: MUHAMMAD,
#   MOHAMMED and MUHAMMED are the same name written differently. This file
#   holds something harder. The same Arabic root is absorbed into different
#   Nigerian languages and comes out phonologically reshaped, so the surface
#   forms diverge far enough that no phonetic encoder will ever connect them:
#       Hebrew Avraham -> Arabic Ibrahim -> Yoruba Buraimoh
#   IBRAHIM and BURAIMOH share almost no consonant skeleton. Double Metaphone
#   gives APRHM and PRM. Jaro-Winkler scores them near zero. Only a table can
#   link them.
#   This also means a name is not always owned by one tradition. Arabic-derived
#   names are shared across Hausa and Yoruba Muslim populations, so a lexicon
#   row saying "hausa" may be describing where the name is most common rather
#   than where a given person's usage sits.
# STATUS
#   One confirmed chain. This file is deliberately almost empty rather than
#   filled with plausible guesses: getting an adaptation wrong links two
#   different people, and I have no basis for asserting these beyond the one
#   that was given to me. Additions want a speaker, not inference.
# Each row is one equivalence group, pipe-separated. Any member matches any
# other member.
